questions.q: What is the difference between a model inventory and a model registry, per this lesson?
options: An inventory is the authoritative list of models; a registry is the system that enforces and maintains that list as models are actually built and served
They are exactly the same thing, just different names for one spreadsheet
An inventory only tracks data, never models
A registry is a one-time report generated for auditors, with no ongoing role
questions.explain: The inventory is the list; the registry is the system that makes registration the only path to production so the list stays accurate on its own.

questions.q: What problem does the lesson compare 'shadow models' to?
options: Shadow IT — unmanaged spreadsheets and databases governance already had to solve for
Credit card fraud
Server downtime
A shortage of data scientists
questions.explain: The lesson draws a direct parallel: untracked models are the same governance problem as untracked spreadsheets and databases, just for ML.

questions.q: In the screenshot example, what does registering a model into Unity Catalog, rather than the legacy Workspace Model Registry, give the model?
options: The same governed catalog.schema.model namespace, owner, and audit trail as a table
A faster training time
Automatic deletion after 30 days
Exemption from any access control
questions.explain: Registering into Unity Catalog puts the model under the same governed namespace and permission model as any other catalog object, instead of a separate ungoverned silo.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does a bare file path and version number fail to capture that a governance-ready registry entry needs?
options: Owner, risk tier, full version history, and a link to the model's documentation
The programming language the model was written in
The physical server rack the model runs on
The name of the first person who ever opened the file
questions.explain: The lesson lists owner, risk tier, version history, current-serving status, and a linked model card as what a real entry needs beyond just a file and version.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say it doesn't matter which specific registry tool (MLflow, Azure ML, SageMaker, Vertex AI) a team uses?
options: What matters for governance is that registering a model is the only supported path to production, regardless of tool
Because none of these tools actually track model versions
Because only one of these tools is a real product
Because governance doesn't apply to machine learning models
questions.explain: The governance requirement is behavioral — registration as the only path to production — not tied to any single vendor's implementation.
